items.claim: The row's back seam at MT 8:5|8:6 is cut inside a continuous 2ms-address chain, with no tier-1 marker at the cut, no tier-3 corroboration, and no disclosure of the straddle.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier at oshb:Song.8.5, and the mi-zot digit is right (skeleton sweep: 3 verses, oshb:Song.3.6, oshb:Song.6.10, oshb:Song.8.5). The defect is the unargued back seam. The verse's second half addresses a 2ms hearer four times over - עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ, חִבְּלַ֣תְךָ, אִמֶּ֔ךָ, יְלָדַֽתְךָ (oshb:Song.8.5, byte tier) - and the same 1cs speaker keeps addressing the same 2ms hearer straight across the seam: שִׂימֵ֨נִי, then עַל לִבֶּ֗ךָ and עַל זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier). Six qamats-final-kaf suffixes straddle the cut and no gender-marked form changes on either side of it, while the parashah layer places nothing at all between MT 8:4 and MT 8:7 (tier-3, single-witness) - so the cut carries neither a tier-1 voice marker nor tier-3 corroboration, and the row's rationale and signals argue only its front seam. Secondary: the epigram warrant appeals to how the book's other ascending-question sites are treated rather than to bytes, and the attested ascent shape is narrower than the 3-verse digit implies - מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר recurs at oshb:Song.3.6 as מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר (skeleton sweep for that run: 2 verses), whereas oshb:Song.6.10 reads מִי זֹ֥את הַנִּשְׁקָפָ֖ה כְּמוֹ שָׁ֑חַר with no ascent language.

skeleton (mi-zot formula sweeps, verse counts)

items.claim: The front seam at MT 8:5|8:6 is labelled a voice shift although speaker and addressee are unchanged across it - what changes is verbal mood - and the straddling 2ms address chain is undisclosed.
items.evidence: Credit first, because the highest-risk item in the cluster is handled correctly: the divided-token pair שַׁלְהֶ֥בֶתְ יָֽה re-collates at byte tier at oshb:Song.8.6, the one-word/divided-token fact and the lemma tag are disclosed, the construal is held rather than decided, the exegesis note is marked single-witness apparatus, and no standalone Yah-form digit is asserted (a naive skeleton sweep for that two-letter string hits 11 verses - the trap is avoided). Two defects remain. (1) The row's only front-seam signal is a 2ms imperative address, but oshb:Song.8.5's second half already runs the identical 1cs-speaker / 2ms-addressee configuration - עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ, חִבְּלַ֣תְךָ, אִמֶּ֔ךָ, יְלָדַֽתְךָ (byte tier) - into עַל לִבֶּ֗ךָ and עַל זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier); no gender-marked form changes at the seam, so what MT 8:5|8:6 attests is a qatal-to-imperative mood shift, not a voice shift, and the straddling address chain goes undisclosed while the rationale supplies no other front-seam evidence. (2) Quote/gloss parity: the gloss 'for love is strong as death' renders כִּֽי (oshb:Song.8.6, byte tier), which stands outside the quoted run עַזָּ֤ה כַמָּ֨וֶת֙ אַהֲבָ֔ה. The back seam (setumah closing MT 8:7) is correctly cited and correctly disclosed single-witness.

items.claim: The rival dialogue reading is rejected on a ground the bytes contest, and the book's only two wall-noun sites sit on either side of the row's own back seam, undisclosed.
items.evidence: The 1cp identification is byte-sound - אָח֥וֹת לָ֨נוּ֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה at byte tier at oshb:Song.8.8, with נַּעֲשֶׂה֙ and לַאֲחֹתֵ֔נוּ there and נִבְנֶ֥ה / נָצ֥וּר at oshb:Song.8.9 - and the little-sister role-split away from the bride-epithet is handled correctly. The defect is the rejected alternative's stated ground, that the span is voiced by one speaker-group 'without an answering party': the answering party is the next verse, and it answers in the same word. That noun occurs in exactly 2 verses in the book (skeleton sweep: oshb:Song.8.9, oshb:Song.8.10), the two are adjacent, and the pair is identical once cantillation is stripped - חוֹמָ֣ה at oshb:Song.8.9 against חוֹמָ֔ה at oshb:Song.8.10 (each byte tier at its own ref, accent-stripped tier as a pair). אִם חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא is answered by אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה, and וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ is answered by וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת (byte tier). A byte-true device straddling the row's own seam argues continuity against that seam unless disclosed; nothing in the row's prose discloses it, even though MT 8:10-8:12 is carried in the evidence refs without ever being argued. The front seam (setumah closing MT 8:7) is correctly cited and single-witness disclosed.

items.claim: The quoted marker is a common-gender pronoun and cannot carry the row's return to her own voice; the verse's actual gender-bearing forms go unquoted, and the petuchah is placed inside the verse rather than at the division it closes.
items.evidence: אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה re-collates at byte tier at oshb:Song.8.10, and the person/number shift away from the 1cp of oshb:Song.8.9 (נִבְנֶ֥ה, נָצ֥וּר, byte tier) is real evidence for a speaker change. But the owner voice policy requires the gender-marked form to be quoted, and אֲנִ֣י is common-gender first person: it fixes person and number, not the speaker's sex, so the form the row quotes does not carry the gender it is asked to carry. The verse's gender-bearing evidence sits in the clauses the row does not quote - כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם, a feminine-singular participle, and בְעֵינָ֖יו, a 3ms suffix locating the other party as a man, alongside וְשָׁדַ֖י answering oshb:Song.8.8 (all oshb:Song.8.10, byte tier). Second defect: the petuchah is a verse-keyed seg that follows the verse it closes, so it corroborates the MT 8:10|8:11 division, not this row's opening; saying it sits exactly at the verse-initial pronoun is an intra-verse position claim the single-witness inventory cannot source, and it lends tier-3 weight to a front seam the mark does not touch. The 1-of-20 digit, the PE-versus-SAMEKH distinction and the single-witness disclosure are otherwise correct.

items.claim: The claim that a 1cs possessive marks her voice throughout is false for MT 8:11, which carries no first-person form at all, and the 1cs forms in MT 8:12 are common-gender - the female attribution rests on cross-verse continuity alone.
items.evidence: Both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier, and the row correctly quotes both attested vineyard spellings across the final-mem allography (כֶּ֣רֶם at oshb:Song.8.11, כָּרְמִ֥י at oshb:Song.8.12). But oshb:Song.8.11 contains no first-person form whatever: its finite verbs are third-person (הָיָ֤ה, נָתַ֥ן, יָבִ֥א) and its only person-marked suffix is 3ms בְּפִרְי֖וֹ (byte tier). In oshb:Song.8.12 the first-person forms כָּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י לְפָנָ֑י are common-gender, and the verse's only person-marked address is 2ms - הָאֶ֤לֶף לְךָ֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה (byte tier) - which the 'her own possessive claim' characterization drops. The attribution therefore rests on continuity carried across verses, which the owner voice policy rates tier-2 corroboration and bars as a sole seam driver, and the replacement warrant offered is an appeal to a category rather than to bytes. Byte evidence that would have carried it is unused: the possessive phrase כָּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י recurs at oshb:Song.1.6 as כַּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י - the phrase's only two sites (skeleton sweep: 2 verses), identical at skeleton tier only, since the first vowel differs - and oshb:Song.1.6 is unambiguously her voice (שֶׁאֲנִ֣י שְׁחַרְחֹ֔רֶת and נֹטֵרָ֣ה, feminine forms, byte tier) as well as the brothers' verse (בְּנֵ֧י אִמִּ֣י), with the keeper lexeme linking oshb:Song.1.6, oshb:Song.8.11 and oshb:Song.8.12 (skeleton sweep: 3 verses). The front seam (petuchah closing MT 8:10) is correctly cited and single-witness disclosed.

items.claim: The row calls gender marking thin and denies an unambiguous vocative, but MT 8:13 and MT 8:14 carry the span's cleanest 2fs/2ms minimal pair together with the policy's first-named tier-1 address word.
items.evidence: oshb:Song.8.13 addresses a woman three times over: הַיוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת, article plus feminine-singular participle standing in vocative position; לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ, whose suffix is tsere plus final kaf plus sheva, the 2fs shape; and הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי, a feminine-singular imperative carrying a 1cs object suffix (all byte tier). oshb:Song.8.14 flips every one of them: בְּרַ֣ח and וּֽדְמֵה are masculine-singular imperatives, לְךָ֤ carries sheva plus final kaf plus qamats, the 2ms shape, and דּוֹדִ֗י is the woman's own address word for the man, which the owner voice policy names first in its tier-1 address vocabulary (sweep: 24 verses in that exact spelling) - an explicit vocative, not an inference from address direction. לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ against לְךָ֤ is a byte-level 2fs/2ms minimal pair across the row's internal seam, so these are the most sharply marked speaker turns in the span, not the thinnest. Holding the two verses as one dialogue_exchange is defensible on the hold-whole ground, but the row's stated warrant - that the markers are too thin to argue a seam - is contested by the bytes, and the confidence band follows from that misstatement. Parity defect in the same field: the gloss 'companions listening for your voice' renders חֲבֵרִ֛ים, which stands outside the quoted run, and that run's first word מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים is a masculine-plural participle agreeing with those companions, so labelling the whole run a 2fs imperative summons misdescribes it.
